hints.content: The opposite angles in ANY inscribed quadrilateral are supplementary.  [[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
The measure of an inscribed angle is $\frac{1}{2}$ of the measure of the arc that it intercepts.

$\pink{\text{m}\angle K} = \frac{1}{2}(\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{DUC})$  
$\blue{\text{m}\angle U} = \frac{1}{2}(\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{CKD})$

When we add the measures of the two angles together, something interesting happens:

$\pink{\text{m}\angle K}+ \blue{\text{m}\angle U} = \frac{1}{2}(\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{DUC}) + \frac{1}{2}(\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{CKD})$

$\pink{\text{m}\angle K} + \blue{\text{m}\angle U} = \frac{1}{2}(\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{DUC} + \text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{CKD})$

The sum of those $2$ arcs makes up the entire circle, which is $360^\circ$.

$\pink{\text{m}\angle K} + \blue{\text{m}\angle U} = \frac{1}{2}(360) = 180$
